llm.summary: This is a transparent self-hosted speech-service skill whose network use, file persistence, and voice-cloning risks are disclosed and aligned with its purpose.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTP, local Docker operation, GPU/large-model resource use, and optional bearer auth are proportionate for a self-hosted speech server, but users must configure network exposure and auth carefully because auth is off by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses Docker images, host data mounts, curl, and optional ffmpeg workflows; these are disclosed and user-run, with no hidden autorun or obfuscated install behavior in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to an operator-chosen TALKIES_URL and include clear warnings to review shell commands, avoid sensitive data on untrusted servers, only delete files staged by the current workflow, and avoid unauthorized voice cloning.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Staged uploads, cached URL downloads, model files, and custom voices persist server-side under the data directory until cleanup; this persistence and shared namespace behavior are repeatedly disclosed with cleanup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: ASR, TTS, streaming, MCP ASR tools, URL download, server-side staging, and voice cloning are coherent with the stated self-hosted speech-service purpose; voice cloning is dual-use but explicitly framed with consent requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the Docker image and the TALKIES_URL server. For anything beyond a private local test, bind to localhost or a protected network, set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, prefer HTTPS behind a proxy, keep debug logging off for real data, clean up staged files and cached downloads, and only use voice-cloning samples with explicit consent.
llm.findings:
[LP4] expected: The declared network permission is not unsupported; the documented workflows repeatedly call the configured TALKIES_URL and explain server-side URL fetching.
[E1] expected: The curl examples transmit audio, text, and voice-cloning inputs to the configured speech server, which is core functionality and is explicitly disclosed as data leaving the host.
[EA2] unexpected: The matched text is an acceptable-use warning requiring speaker consent for voice cloning, not an instruction to make autonomous high-impact decisions.
